title: Leveraging Quantum Computing and Optimization to Estimate Financial Crashes in Small and Medium-Sized Enterprises
journal_or_venue: 2024 9th International Conference on Computer Science and Engineering (UBMK)
abstract_summary: The paper formulates a quadratically constrained quadratic optimization model to estimate financial crashes in a network of SMEs by encoding dependencies such as cross-holdings, self-holdings, asset ownership and failure costs. Because the resulting NP-hard problem is intractable classically, the authors leverage D-Wave hybrid quantum solvers (CQM) to find equilibria rapidly and report high detection of non-performing loans on 2019–2020 data, with solutions obtained in seconds rather than infeasible classical runtimes.
methodology_description: The authors formulate financial-crash estimation for a network of SME customers as a quadratically constrained quadratic optimization problem that models inter-firm debt relations as cross-holdings. They build a directed weighted financial network from trial balances and balance sheets (receivables/payables become edges) and compute parameters such as crossholding ratios Cij, self-holdings Ĉii, asset ownership proportions Dik, market prices pk, book values Vi and a dependency matrix A = Ĉ (I − C)^{-1}. A discrete integer/binary decision model is used: integer market-value variables vi and binary failure indicators yi, with an objective minimizing sum_i (vi − Ĉii (sum_j≠i Cij Vj + sum_k Dik pk − βi(p) yi))^2 subject to logical constraints linking vi and yi and integrality bounds. Preprocessing converts floating-point financial numbers to integers by scaling (multiply by 10^{max_decimal_places}). The constrained quadratic model (CQM) is solved using D-Wave’s Hybrid CQM solvers (quantum annealing + classical components). Experiments use repeated runs (five repeats) to explore multiple equilibrium points, with a recommended solver time of ~7 seconds per run. Postprocessing maps predicted failed firms to real-world unpaid-debt outcomes (future quarters) and evaluates the coverage of actual non-performing loans (reported as TL amounts and percent coverage).
frameworks: D-Wave Hybrid Solver (Constrained Quadratic Model - CQM)
experimental_setup: Problem formulated as a constrained quadratic model (integer vi, binary yi) solved with D-Wave hybrid CQM solver. Floating point financial values scaled to integers by multiplying by 10^{max_decimal_places}. Each experiment repeated 5 times to sample multiple equilibrium points; recommended hybrid solve time ~7 seconds per run. Postprocessing compares predicted failing firms to real unpaid-debt amounts in subsequent reporting quarters.
dataset_used: Proprietary financial records (trial balances and balance sheets) of Yapı Kredi Bank SME customers for 2019–2020. Selection: customers whose Strategic Business Unit (SBU) segment remained unchanged between 01-01-2019 and 31-12-2020. Features include cash & equivalents, securities, trade receivables, financial liabilities, trade payables, advances received, total equity, and pairwise payables/receivables (to form network edges). Dataset sizes (number of firms) are not specified in the paper.

pipeline_steps: Construct directed financial network from trial balance/payable-receivable relations.

Compute model parameters: crossholding ratios Cij, self-holdings Ĉii, asset ownership Dik, market prices pk, book values Vi, unit liquidation costs λik, failure-cost functions βi(p), threshold values vCi, dependency matrix A = Ĉ (I − C)^{-1}.
Formulate constrained quadratic optimization: minimize sum_i (vi − Ĉii(sum_j≠i Cij Vj + sum_k Dik pk − βi(p) yi))^2 subject to logical constraints linking vi and yi, yi ∈ {0,1}, vi ∈ {0,1,…,vmax_i}.
Preprocess numeric data to integers (scale by 10^{max_decimals}).
Solve the CQM with D-Wave hybrid solver (quantum annealing + classical hybrid components), using recommended solve time (~7s).
Repeat optimization 5 times to sample different equilibrium solutions due to multiple equilibria and solver randomness.

Postprocess solutions: map yi=1 firms to predicted unpaid debt amounts, propagate effects via dependency matrix to observe cascade effects, and compare predicted unpaid debt totals against observed real unpaid debt in future quarters.

results_summary: The authors developed a constrained quadratic optimization model (CQM) to estimate financial crashes in an SME network and solved it using D-Wave's hybrid solvers. They preprocessed financial data (integer encoding), repeated runs to explore multiple equilibria, and evaluated model outputs against real unpaid-debt records. Empirical runs reported feasible solutions in ≈7 seconds and identified substantial portions of known NPLs: about 90M TL of ~107M TL (2019) and about 669.92M TL of ~726M TL (2020). The work emphasizes cascading default dynamics, the need to handle multiple equilibria, and argues for quantum or hybrid quantum-classical methods as a practical way to tackle such NP-hard financial-network problems.

quantum_advantage_detail: The authors report empirical hybrid-solver runtimes (~7 s) and cite literature claiming infeasibility for classical methods (~13.7 billion years). However, the solution uses D-Wave's hybrid (quantum+classical) solver, the classical vs. quantum comparison is taken from prior theoretical work, and no controlled classical-baseline benchmark on the same instance is provided in this paper; therefore the claim of concrete quantum advantage is presented but remains speculative rather than demonstrated.
limitations: Multiple equilibrium points in the optimization problem require repeated runs and post-processing to identify banking-feasible solutions (authors stated).
Incomplete observability of firms' outside-network assets/receivables means some mathematically-viable equilibria are not realistic in practice and require manual filtering (authors stated).

Evaluation relies on matching model-indicated crash firms to real unpaid-debt amounts rather than standard ML metrics (precision/recall) because ground truth for equilibria is incomplete (authors stated).

Quantum hybrid solver randomness and multiple possible equilibria necessitated repeating experiments (5 times) to sample different optima; shorter solve times produced infeasible (constraint-violating) solutions (authors stated).

QPU / solver input restrictions forced numeric preprocessing (elimination of floating-point numbers via scaling), which increases magnitudes and may introduce numerical/representation limitations (authors stated).

The dataset lacks market values and equity-share crossholdings (SMEs are private), so receivables/payables were reinterpreted as crossholding-like relations — a modeling approximation (authors stated).
Network excludes large companies; authors note including larger firms would make projections more realistic (authors stated).

contradictions: The paper asserts that the D-Wave hybrid solver finds solutions 'rapidly' and that classical runtimes would be infeasible, yet it provides no empirical classical-solver baseline or head-to-head runtime/solution-quality comparison on the same dataset, undermining the strength of the quantum-advantage claim.

Problem size details (number of firms, number of variables/qubits, constraint counts) are not reported; claiming scalability or practical superiority is contradicted by the absence of evidence about how the approach scales to larger, real-world networks.

Results come from a hybrid (quantum + classical) solver but the contribution of the quantum component versus the classical components is not quantified; therefore claims of quantum superiority are not clearly substantiated and could be driven largely by classical processing.
